# The Forge — Fractional CFO Action Plan

## INCREASE REVENUE

- **Pricing audit urgent.** AR/M (average revenue per member) has collapsed from £170.43 (Dec) to £120.48 (June) to £9.03 (July). July's figure is clearly corrupted data or a severe billing/booking system failure — investigate immediately. Even June at £120.48 is 29% down on December. You have 147–151 active members but pricing or package mix has deteriorated. Audit what members are paying; implement tiered pricing (foundation/premium/VIP) and shift low-margin tiers upward by 8–12%.
- **Churn control is critical.** April–June saw attrition spike to 8.33%, 5.74%, and 0% (June anomaly). Pre-relocation (Sep–Nov) you averaged 2.5%. Bigger studio should reduce attrition, not spike it. Introduce a 30-day onboarding touchpoint, monthly 1-to-1 check-ins with at-risk members, and a 90-day retention bonus. Every 1% churn reduction on 147 members saves £1,800–£2,000 annually.
- **Upsell PT and class packages.** Non-peak hours (off-peak classes, quieter slots) likely have spare capacity in the larger studio. Bundle group fitness or intro PT sessions with membership upgrades. Target 15% of members into a mid-tier plan; at current member count, that's £4,500+/month incremental revenue.

## REDUCE EXPENSES

- **Non-people expenses are out of control.** June (£9,390) and March (£15,639) are 2–3× baseline (Sep–Nov averaged £4,540). April's relocation justifies one spike, but June remains 106% above September. Audit rent/utilities (did lease or rates increase post-move?), software/subscriptions, repairs, and insurance. Target: bring non-people costs down to £5,500–£6,000/month (30% of revenue). That alone recovers £3,000–£4,000 monthly profit.
- **People costs are stable but rising.** Payroll grew from £2,763 (Sep) to £3,686 (June) — a 33% increase. You've added ~60 members (+71%) but headcount growth may be misaligned. Assess whether you need fixed staff increases or can shift to contractor/part-time PT model for some roles. Aim to keep people costs at 18–20% of revenue;

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling first** — Before writing anything, have your coaches list every service variation they currently offer (1:1 PT sessions, group classes, nutrition consults, form checks, etc.). You'll find inconsistencies and pricing gaps that are costing you money. This takes 2 hours max and prevents building a menu on fiction.

• **Price backwards from member willingness-to-pay, not cost-plus guessing** — Survey 10-15 existing members: "What would you pay for [specific service]?" Use those actual numbers, not what you think sounds reasonable. Women's fitness has different value perception than generic gyms—lean into that.

• **Create two separate, brutally simple documents** — Coach menu (what they can offer, how to position it, upsell triggers) vs. member menu (benefits-focused pricing tiers, bundled packages that look like deals). Don't make coaches read member marketing language; they need operational clarity.

• **Build in decision rules for your coaches** — When can they offer X service for free (trial, loyalty)? When must they upsell Y? Document this NOW so you're not having daily conversations about what they can discount. This saves time and protects margins.

• **Use your menu as a sales tool immediately** — Print it, share digitally, train coaches to reference it during consultations. If you're not using it within 48 hours to close sales or clarify offerings to members, it's just a document.

What's your current pricing variance across your coaches?
